The Big Story · Society & History

Japan’s Olympic holiday moved. Then its name changed.

October 10 once fixed a national day to Tokyo 1964. Japan is off work today, October 12—and the gap explains two quiet rewrites of the country’s sporting identity.

Today’s Japan

Sports Day · Essential read

The date moved. The meaning widened.

Sports Day began as an October 10 memorial to Tokyo 1964. The second-Monday rule and a new legal name turned that fixed anniversary into something broader.

Animation · Final day

Thirty-four schools. Two hundred twenty-nine films. No single “anime style.”

ICAF 2026 closes at the National Art Center, Tokyo today, revealing experimental work before Japan’s commercial animation pipeline.

02
Health · Tokyo event

Japan is asking families to discuss medical decisions before a crisis.

A Ministry of Health event today promotes jinsei kaigi—advance care planning: repeated conversations about care a person would want if they could no longer explain it themselves.

Music · Odaiba

A three-day festival closes with part of the show streaming beyond the venue.

BMSG FES ’26 ends today in Odaiba. The organizer announced limited official livestreaming and a paid three-day Prime Video PPV feed.

Kimono · Final day

Kimono is being presented as a living content industry.

Japanese word of the dayスポーツの日 · supōtsu no hi

Japan’s official name for Sports Day. 日 means “day,” while スポーツ renders “sports.” Example: Kyō wa Supōtsu no Hi desu—“Today is Sports Day.” A school athletic festival is usually undōkai. Learn distinctions like this while playing with DraMap.
